summary: The note surveys strategies communities have adopted since September 2023 to bring young people into local decision-making, drawing on forums, workshops and initiatives between September 2023 and February 2024. Strategies include Youth Advisory Councils, civic education with internships, the CiviConnect app, mentorship, youth project grants, town halls, social media campaigns, inclusive representation, and ongoing evaluation. Each is illustrated by a named speaker or local example.
one_line: Overview of ten strategies, from youth advisory councils to feedback systems, for involving young people in local governance, with examples from 2023-2024 events.
key_facts: Stephanie Richards, a youth advocate, gave the keynote at a forum on September 15, 2023, arguing that young people bring fresh perspectives and are acutely affected by current policies.
Councilman James Aguilar of Springfield described the city's Youth Advisory Council (YAC) at a workshop on October 3, 2023; YACs let youths advise officials on issues affecting their demographic.
On October 21, 2023, a panel of educators and school board members discussed integrating civic education into the school curriculum.
Lisa McDaniel, a high school social studies teacher, said her school partnered with local government offices to provide internships and shadowing opportunities for students.

Tech entrepreneur Kevin Chen presented the app "CiviConnect" at a digital innovation summit on November 8, 2023; it sends alerts on local issues, simplifies legislation summaries and offers tools for contacting representatives or submitting public comments.

Former mayor Patricia Gomez launched a leadership mentorship program on November 30, 2023, pairing experienced politicians and civic servants with youth interested in public service; she personally mentors two college students.

On December 12, 2023, the city of Oakridge announced a grants program funding initiatives designed and executed by young people; councilwoman Angela Pearson said it instills responsibility and ownership.
Regional youth listening sessions concluded on January 5, 2024, inviting young residents to share concerns and suggestions, including the most marginalized youth.
The city of Brookfield launched a social media campaign on January 20, 2024 using Instagram and TikTok to educate youth on local issues and civic events.
Maria Gonzalez, Brookfield's Director of Communications, said "These platforms are where the youth are, and we need to meet them there."
Diversity advocate Brian Chang held a session called 'Inclusive Youth Engagement' on February 11, 2024, arguing diverse representation leads to richer discussions and more equitable decisions.
Researcher Malcolm White presented a paper on February 22, 2024 stressing the need for ongoing feedback and evaluation systems to keep youth-engagement strategies dynamic and responsive.
